scorecards.inningsCommentary: India commenced their first innings at Melbourne Cricket Ground, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 106 from Cheteshwar Pujara, complemented by a commanding 170-run stand between Virat Kohli and Cheteshwar Pujara that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.61 RPO. Australia's bowling response was spearheaded by Pat Cummins (3/72), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Finishing at 443/7 (169.4 ov), India established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Melbourne Cricket Ground commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 443/7 (169.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Australia countered with 151/10 (66.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Pat Cummins (6/26), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Pat Cummins delivered a masterclass for Australia (80 Runs & 9 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 53%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Australia faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by Jasprit Bumrah (9 Wickets), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 137 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Australia produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
